pr_comments:
There was a limitation that TIFF input/output with added depth must be 1 channel.It is not documented.

Indirectly cvtColor() gives an error that unsupported depth is entered. This is a confusing error for imread/imwrite users.

As a related work, 3/4 channel will be supported at this fix.

issue_context.title: signed 32bit tiff file writing with compression
issue_context.body:
### System Information

OpenCV python version: 4.7.0.72
Operating System / Platform: Windows 10
Python version: 3.10.10


### Detailed description

Writing a signed 32 bit image as a tiff file will not be compressed with LZW. Not by default or when explicitly asked with a flag.

### Steps to reproduce

```py
import cv2
import numpy as np

cv2.imwrite('gray8.tiff', np.zeros(shape=(1000,1000), dtype=np.int8), (cv2.IMWRITE_TIFF_COMPRESSION, 5))  # 5 is LZW compression
cv2.imwrite('gray32.tiff', np.zeros(shape=(1000,1000), dtype=np.int32), (cv2.IMWRITE_TIFF_COMPRESSION, 5))  # 5 is LZW compression
```

Checking the files afterwards, 'gray8.tiff' is compressed with LZW, while 'gray32.tiff' isn't

### Issue submission checklist

- [X] I report the issue, it's not a question
- [X] I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, forum.opencv.org, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found any solution
- [X] I updated to the latest OpenCV version and the issue is still there
- [X] There is reproducer code and related data files (videos, images, onnx, etc)
comments:
I think it is a opencv bug, it is better to support CV_32S images with LZW compression.

I saw https://github.com/opencv/opencv/pull/21428 . 
But I couldn't read why the CV_32S image had to be uncompressed.

https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/352f92e4373fd4f7b61e1f1ae6aae064f2a3a6ef/modules/imgcodecs/src/grfmt_tiff.cpp#L1282-L1290

+++ b/modules/imgcodecs/src/grfmt_tiff.cpp
@@ -1279,13 +1279,18 @@ bool TiffEncoder::writeLibTiff( const std::vector<Mat>& img_vec, const std::vect
                 break;
             }

-            case CV_32F:
-                sample_format = SAMPLEFORMAT_IEEEFP;
-                /* FALLTHRU */
             case CV_32S:
+            {
+                bitsPerChannel = 32;
+                sample_format = SAMPLEFORMAT_UINT;
+                break;
+            }
+
+            case CV_32F:
             {
                 bitsPerChannel = 32;
                 page_compression = COMPRESSION_NONE;

                 break;
             }

review_comments: Technically, you can use `cv::split` to decompose the image on planes and cv::merge to assemble them in any order you want. Single piece of code should cover all missing types. In case if, let's say `CV_16S` is mot supported by one if functions, you can cast it it CV_16U, do permutations and cast back.

Thank you for your comment! 

 I thought splitting from Src to 3 planes(B/G/R) with `cv::split` and merging 3 planes to Dst with `cv::merge` use more memory/computing resource. 

I referenced OpenCV manual again. I think cv::mixChannels is suitable to this purpose. I think this cost result is acceptable.

(This results are tested under virtual machine)
- src image is 1920x1080, a half of upper is random, a harf of lower is 0-filled. 
- Value is the medium value of 10 trials.
- Time contains create src image, encode to buffer and decode to dst image.
- unis is "mill sec"
- If (b)/(a) is smaller, Copy from Src to Dst is faster than mixChannel.
